recipes.name: Homemade Apple Juice
ingredients_raw: 3 peels and cores from red apples - seeds removed

steps.text: Combine water with apple peels and cores in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the apple flavor and color have permeated the water, about 30 minutes.
Strain apple juice into a mixing bowl; discard all solids. Stir in sugar until dissolved. Allow to cool for 30 minutes before drinking.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Apple Juice
raw_recipe.description: Apple juice is easy to make at home with his clever recipe that simmers apple peels and cores, water, and sugar for a light and refreshing drink.

review.reviewBody: love this recipe...i did adjust it alittle however. I used the whole apple but cored it. boiled for an hour and took some advice and let it soak in the fidge over night..I did add 1/3 cup of cugar because my apples werent that sweet. My 5 month old loves it!!! Thanks very much!!!!

I made this & it was absolutely amazing! I used the peels & deseeded cores from 4 Suncrisps (yellow) & 2 Honeycrisps (red) apples. I did the 5 cups of water & reduced the sugar to about 1/4 cup (as these apples tend to be very sweet already). I cooked the peels & cores on high for about 45 mins & then strained everything from the juice several times in order to get the juice as pure as possible. Then I added the sugar and mixed until dissolved & let it sit for about 10-15 minutes to cool. I then poured over ice & served it to my family who all loved it as much as I did! We do the whole apple picking thing every year as a family & I make homemade applesauce & pies & usually throw all the cores & peels away....well no more! Going forward I will be using them to make this delicious apple juice for my family! ????
This is excellent I used green apples and the sour sweet taste is amazing. I used cores and skin and it's Def very flavorful not bland at all but I boiled it for 45 min

I loved it! Kids loved it! The only things I changed: 1) I lowered amount of sugar which I do with store bought juice by watering it down anyway. Kids are used to not so sweet juice. 2) I drained (filtered) the grainy apple and sugar particles. This made the juice I served the kids completely liquid free of any bits of anything. It comes out white at first, but if you let it sit , it eventually gets darker in color due to oxygenation, just like a normal apple would. Still delicious! Thank you for the recipe !!!

Nice recipe. I added a bit of a cinnamon stick in it while boiling. Idk why, but I like that flavour in apple juice. Also, may be a little less sugar if the apples are sweet. One question: what to do with the boiled apple core remnants? I don't want to throw it away!

great recipe! I modified it to suit me and it was perfect. I boiled for 45min 5 bruised apples that fell on the ground from my tree. added half the sugar and it was great. my whole family loved it. I am making it again the next morning and sharing on fb. Thank u for sharing!

This is a great idea to use up the bits you would otherwise waste and I suspect that the apple variety used makes a huge difference, but I used the cores and peels from 4 pink lady apples in 4 cups of water and it tasted quite insipid after an hour of simmering and definitely didn't need any sugar. I ended up leaving the pot to sit overnight and it was like slightly diluted juice in the morning. I'll make this again, but with a higher ratio of peel to water for a really appple-ey flavour.
